about.title: San Francisco Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Most of what goes wrong in a San Francisco home, garage, or workplace never makes the news. A space heater in a Mission Street flat shorts out. An e-bike battery charging overnight catches fire. A pressure cooker lid gives way, a ladder buckles, a child's toy splinters. When a product fails the person using it as intended, California law treats that failure differently from an ordinary accident. Under strict product liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product had a defect — in its design, in how it was made, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. Everyone in the chain that brought the item to San Francisco County can share responsibility: the maker, the distributor, and the retailer who sold it. We handle product liability claims on a contingency basis, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why San Francisco Residents Choose Us for Product Claims

items.title: Strict liability shifts the focus to the product
items.desc: In California, you usually do not have to prove the company was negligent. Our team can help you show the product was defective and that the defect caused your harm — which is a different, more focused task than a typical injury case.

items.title: The product is your evidence, and it needs protecting
items.desc: Do not throw it away, return it, or let it be repaired. We can guide you on storing the item, its packaging, receipts, and any photos so nothing is lost before it can be examined.

items.title: More than one company may owe you an answer
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the store that sold the item can all be held responsible under California law. We review the full chain from factory to your front door in San Francisco County.

items.question: I was in a crash on US-101 and I think a part of my car failed. Is that a product case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Many San Francisco collisions on corridors like US-101, I-80, and Mission Street are treated as ordinary traffic cases, but if a tire, airbag, brake, or seatbelt did not perform as designed, a product liability claim against the manufacturer may exist alongside any claim against another driver. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until it can be inspected. Our team can sort out which claims apply.

items.question: I bought the product online and it shipped to my apartment. Can I still bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, yes. California's strict liability rules apply to products sold to residents here regardless of whether you bought them in a storefront or from an online retailer. Sellers and distributors, not only the manufacturer, may be responsible. Save your order confirmation, the shipping box, and any listing screenshots you can find.

items.question: Do you charge me anything?
items.answer: No. We handle your claim on contingency, which means we are paid a percentage of any recovery and you owe no attorney fee if there is none.
